## Introduction

```{r Setup}
options(scipen=999) #turns off scientific notation for numbers. 
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width=12, fig.height=8) #knit to word, pdf  chops titles and graphs without setting the figure size as the global option.

library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(caret)
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
setwd("C:\\Users\\star-\\Data Science\\R stuff\\D.comm")

#import statements
#modeldf<-read.csv("C:\\Users\\star-\\Data Science\\R stuff\\D.comm\\modeldf.csv")
modeldf<-read_xlsx("C:\\Users\\star-\\Data Science\\R stuff\\D.comm\\modeldf.xlsx")
summary(modeldf$Associates)
summary(modeldf$Bachelors)
summary(modeldf$Masters)
summary(modeldf$Doctoral)

df<-modeldf|>
  mutate(
    Associates_Percent = (Associates/`Student Count`)*100,
    Bachelors_Percent = (Bachelors/`Student Count`)*100,
    Masters_Percent = (Masters/`Student Count`)*100,
    Doctoral_Percent = (Doctoral/`Student Count`)*100
  )
summary(df$Associates)
summary(df$Associates_Percent)
summary(df$Bachelors_Percent)
summary(df$Masters_Percent)
summary(df$Doctoral_Percent)
```

Analysis of Newly Created Variables

```{r Univariate}
bins = seq(0,100,by=5)
df2<-modeldf|>select(-Institution)|>
  mutate(
    Associates_Percent = (Associates/`Student Count`)*100,
    Bachelors_Percent = (Bachelors/`Student Count`)*100,
    Masters_Percent = (Masters/`Student Count`)*100,
    Doctoral_Percent = (Doctoral/`Student Count`)*100
  )|>filter(Associates_Percent>0,Bachelors_Percent>0,Masters_Percent>0,
   Doctoral_Percent>0,!is.na(Associates_Percent), 
   !is.na(Bachelors_Percent),!is.na(Masters_Percent), !is.na(Doctoral_Percent))


df2|>ggplot(aes(x=Associates_Percent))+geom_histogram(binwidth = 5)
df2|>ggplot(aes(x=Associates))+geom_histogram(binwidth =1500)

df2|>ggplot(aes(x=Bachelors_Percent))+geom_histogram(binwidth = 5)
df2|>ggplot(aes(x=Bachelors))+geom_histogram(binwidth =5000)

df2|>ggplot(aes(x=Masters_Percent))+geom_histogram(binwidth = 5)
df2|>ggplot(aes(x=Masters))+geom_histogram(binwidth =4000)
df2|>ggplot(aes(x=Doctoral_Percent))+geom_histogram(binwidth = 5)
df2|>ggplot(aes(x=Doctoral))+geom_histogram(binwidth =400)
```

## Model 1 and 2: Tree and KNN

### Associates

```{r Associates Split}
df_filter<-df|>filter(Associates_Percent>0)|> select(Associates_Percent,`In-State Tuition`, `Out-of-State Tutition`, `Supply Costs`, `On-Campus Housing`, `On-Campus Expenses`, `Off-Campus Housing`, `Off-Campus Expenses`, `Family Expenses`)|>drop_na()

# test-train split
set.seed(394)


df_trn_idx = sample(nrow(df_filter), size = 0.8 * nrow(df_filter))
df_trn = df_filter[df_trn_idx, ]
df_tst = df_filter[-df_trn_idx, ]
# estimation-validation split
df_est_idx = sample(nrow(df_trn), size = 0.8 * nrow(df_trn))
df_est = df_trn[df_est_idx, ]
df_val = df_trn[-df_est_idx, ]


# check data
head(df_trn, n = 10)

calc_rmse = function(actual, predicted) {
  sqrt(mean((actual - predicted) ^ 2))
}
```

```{r Tree Associates}
tree <- rpart(Associates_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+
                `Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0001))
printcp(tree)

rpart.plot(tree)

#identify best cp value to use
best <- tree$cptable[which.min(tree$cptable[,"xerror"]),"CP"]
best
#produce a pruned tree based on the best cp value
pruned_tree <- prune(tree, cp=best)

#plot the pruned tree
prp(pruned_tree,
    faclen=0, #use full names for factor labels
    extra=1, #display number of obs. for each terminal node
    roundint=F, #don't round to integers in output
    digits=5) #display 5 decimal places in output


tree_mod_list = list(
  tree_0000 <- rpart(Associates_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+`Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0000)),
  tree_0001 <- rpart(Associates_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+ `Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0001)),
  tree_0010 <- rpart(Associates_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+`Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0010)),
  tree_0100 <- rpart(Associates_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+`Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0100))
)

tree_val_pred = lapply(tree_mod_list, predict, df_val)

sapply(tree_val_pred, calc_rmse, df_val$Associates_Percent)
crdt_tree_all = rpart(Associates_Percent ~ ., data = df_est)
rpart.plot(crdt_tree_all)

predict(crdt_tree_all, df_val[1:5, ])
```

```{r Associates KNN}
x<- df_val|>select(-Associates_Percent)
y <- df_val$Associates_Percent

any(is.na(x))

# Fit the KNN regression model
df_knn_15 <- knnreg(x = x, y = y,data=df_est, k = 15)
knn_mod_list = list(
  df_knn_5 <- knnreg(x = x, y = y,data=df_est, k = 5),
  df_knn_10 <- knnreg(x = x, y = y,data=df_est, k = 10),
  df_knn_15<-df_knn_15,
  df_knn_25 <- knnreg(x = x, y = y,data=df_est, k = 25),
  df_knn_50 <- knnreg(x = x, y = y,data=df_est, k = 50),
  df_knn_100 <- knnreg(x = x, y = y,data=df_est, k = 100)
)
head(df_knn_15$learn$X)
dist(head(df_knn_15$learn$X))


#predict(df_knn_10, df_val[1:5, ])
x_val <- df_val |> select(-Associates_Percent)
#glimpse(x_est)
knn_val_pred = lapply(knn_mod_list, predict, x_val)
calc_rmse = function(actual, predicted) {
  sqrt(mean((actual - predicted) ^ 2))
}

sapply(knn_val_pred, calc_rmse, df_val$Associates_Percent)
```

```{r Bachelors Tree}
    faclen=0, #use full names for factor labels

  tree_0000 <- rpart(Bachelors_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+`Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0000)),
  tree_0001 <- rpart(Bachelors_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+ `Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0001)),
  tree_0010 <- rpart(Bachelors_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+`Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0010)),
  tree_0100 <- rpart(Bachelors_Percent ~`In-State Tuition`+ `Out-of-State Tutition`+ `Supply Costs`+`On-Campus Housing`+ `On-Campus Expenses`+ `Off-Campus Housing`+`Off-Campus Expenses`+ `Family Expenses`, data=df_est, control=rpart.control(cp=.0100))
)

tree_val_pred = lapply(tree_mod_list, predict, df_val)

sapply(tree_val_pred, calc_rmse, df_val$Bachelors_Percent)
crdt_tree_all = rpart(Bachelors_Percent ~ ., data = df_est)
rpart.plot(crdt_tree_all)

predict(crdt_tree_all, df_val[1:5, ])
```


## Further Model Building
